clues.title: Google car: blurred red or white pickup
text: The Generation 4 coverage was captured with **red** and **white** pickup trucks, which have been well blurred.
clues.summary: Gen 4 coverage was taken with red and white pickup trucks, both heavily blurred.

clues.title: Google car: white car, long antenna
text: The Generation 3 Google car in Iceland is a **white** **car** with a **long antenna**.
clues.summary: The Gen 3 car is white with a long antenna.

clues.title: Plate: all white, blue letters, no blue strip
text: Icelandic licence plates are **fully white with blue characters**. Unlike most of Europe, the plates do not feature a blue strip on the left.
It can be hard to see the blue of the characters through the blur of the plates.
clues.summary: Fully white plates with blue characters and no blue strip on the left, unlike most of Europe. The blue letters can be hard to see through the blur.

clues.title: Bollard: yellow post, white reflector
text: Iceland has unique **yellow bollards **with a white reflector. These bollards are extremely common and can be found throughout the country on almost every section of rural road.
clues.summary: Yellow bollards with a white reflector. Extremely common on almost every rural road.

clues.title: Landscape: barren, treeless, dark volcanic soil
text: Iceland often looks **barren and treeless**. Most regions have a dark grey soil consisting mostly of volcanic rocks.
NOTE: Due to the lack of trees, the landscape in Iceland does not look like anywhere else in Northern Europe.
clues.summary: Often barren and treeless, with dark grey soil made mostly of volcanic rock. It looks unlike anywhere else in northern Europe.

clues.title: Landscape: rugged volcanic scenery
text: Iceland is a very **geologically active** country, where plate tectonics and volcanic processes have shaped the landscape. As a result, many regions are rugged, mountainous and a sight to behold. In addition, strange and bewildering landscapes can be found all over, such as geothermal lakes, lava fields, rift valleys, and towering rock formations.
clues.summary: A very volcanically active land, so look for rugged mountains, geothermal lakes, lava fields, rift valleys and towering rock formations.

clues.title: Sign: yellow direction signs, white number box
text: The road direction signs of Iceland are **yellow**. They usually have a white inset box that shows the road numbers. If the inset box has a dashed border, the number listed refers to a nearby road, not the road you are currently on.
NOTE: Direction signs for very local destinations, such as farmsteads, typically have different background colours: blue or white.
clues.summary: Yellow direction signs, usually with a white box showing road numbers. A dashed box border means the number is a nearby road, not yours. Local farm signs are blue or white.

clues.title: Sign: pedestrian sign, four stripes, yellow tint
text: Icelandic pedestrian signs feature **four stripes** and often have a **slight yellow tint**.
NOTE: Iceland is the only European country that uses pedestrian signs with a yellow background.
clues.summary: Pedestrian signs show four stripes and often a slight yellow tint. It is the only European country with a yellow pedestrian sign.

clues.title: Language: ð, þ, æ and accented vowels
text: The Icelandic language contains a couple of **unique letters**. These are some of the most recognizable ones: ð þ and æ. Vowels can have the following accents: á é í ó ö ú ý. The uppercase version of ð is Ð.
NOTE: ð is also found in the Faroese language. æ is found in Danish, Norwegian and Faroese.

images.caption: Icelandic text with the letters Á É Í Ó Ú Ý Ö Æ Ð Þ shown large

clues.summary: Special letters ð, þ and æ, plus accented vowels á é í ó ö ú ý. The Faroese language also has ð, and æ appears in Danish, Norwegian and Faroese.

differs.how: Faroese uses ø and lacks þ, é and ö

clues.title: Street sign: white, black text, thin rim
text: Iceland’s street signs use a white background and black text. They often have a **thin metal rim** and are attached to lampposts or traffic lights.
clues.summary: White street signs with black text and often a thin metal rim, fixed to lampposts or traffic lights.

clues.title: Road lines: all white, no yellow
text: Iceland has **all-white** road lines. Outside lines, if present, can be either solid or, more rarely, dashed lines.
NOTE: Iceland has no yellow road lines. If you see yellow road lines in a Nordic environment, consider Norway or Finland.
clues.summary: All-white road lines, with outer lines solid or rarely dashed. There are no yellow lines. Yellow lines in a Nordic setting point to Norway or Finland.

clues.title: Chevron: black with yellow arrows
text: Icelandic chevrons are **black with yellow arrows**.
NOTE: Norway and Finland have similarly coloured chevrons. Sweden, on the other hand, has unique blue and yellow chevrons.
clues.summary: Black chevrons with yellow arrows. Norway and Finland look the same. Sweden has unique blue and yellow chevrons.

differs.how: Swedish chevrons are blue and yellow

clues.title: Sign: yellow-background warning signs
text: Just like Sweden and Finland, Icelandic signs feature a **yellow background**.
clues.summary: Warning signs have a yellow background. Sweden and Finland do the same.

clues.title: Coverage: sparse, dense in the southwest
text: Iceland is rather sparsely covered. The southwest region has the densest coverage. Only a few interior roads are covered.

_You can click on the image to enlarge it. Alternatively, you can look at the coverage in more detail [on this site](https://sv-map.netlify.app#base=roadmap&cov=official&zoom=7&center=65.0373021778563%2C-18.04504783126836)._
clues.summary: Coverage is sparse. The southwest is densest and only a few interior roads are covered.

clues.title: Route numbers: first digit shows region
text: Iceland has a very sensible **road numbering system** that allows for quick 5k’s, provided you find the yellow direction signs that list the road numbers of the intersection you are on.
The main ring road, which circles the entire island, simply has the number 1. There are no other roads that start with 1.

The first digit of the other road numbers is region-specific. These regions have a sequential distribution around the island, starting from 2 in the south and increasing up until 9 in a clockwise direction (see map for approximate distribution).
clues.summary: On yellow direction signs, road number 1 is the ring road around the island. For other roads the first digit is a region, going clockwise from 2 in the south up to 9.

clues.title: Landscape: narrow fjords, flat-topped mountains
text: The Westfjords region features numerous narrow fjords, surrounded by moderately tall, and mostly **flat-topped** mountains.
clues.summary: In the north-west: many narrow fjords with moderately tall, mostly flat-topped mountains around them.

clues.title: Landscape: fjords with big jagged mountains
text: The far east of the country is also home to several fjords. What distinguishes them from the Westfjords are the generally larger and more **jagged mountains**.
clues.summary: In the far east: several fjords, but with larger and more jagged mountains than in the north-west.

clues.title: Landscape: snowy peaks and north-facing valleys
text: The mountains west of Akureyri contain many valleys, sandwiched between tall, often slightly snowcapped peaks. Most of these valleys generally face north to northeast.
clues.summary: West of the biggest northern town: valleys squeezed between tall, often snowcapped peaks, most facing north to north-east.

clues.title: Landscape: dark volcanic gravel, no life
text: Barren landscapes consisting mostly of** dark volcanic gravel**, with little to no vegetation or signs of life, are typical of the inland regions of Iceland. Most such covered roads are located in the east.
clues.summary: Inland: barren dark volcanic gravel with almost no plants. Most covered roads like this are in the east.

clues.title: Landscape: flat farmland, distant mountains
text: The Southwest agricultural area in Iceland can be identified by its relatively flat **farmland landscape** scattered with numerous [farmsteads](https://goo.gl/maps/a8wo7RuEwy7EX5vZ6), fields, meadows and grasslands.
NOTE: Although there are other smaller agricultural areas in Iceland, mountains in this area tend to be quite distant, making it unique.
clues.summary: In the south-west: fairly flat farmland dotted with farmsteads, fields and meadows. The mountains here sit far away, which is unusual.

clues.title: Landscape: wide hilly farm valley, snowy peaks
text: The **wide valley** around Eiðar is slightly hilly and agricultural, with tall, **snowy peaks visible in the distance** on either side, to the east and northwest, respectively.
clues.summary: A wide, slightly hilly farm valley with tall snowy peaks in the distance on both sides, to the east and north-west.

clues.title: Landscape: wooded valley with wide river
text: The valley around Hallormsstaður has a distinct northeast/southwest angle with **low-lying mountains** on either side, a **wide river** flowing through it, and an **unusual amount of trees** for Iceland. Some of the sideroads are [in the forests](https://maps.app.goo.gl/HrmHr9Y8mPom7qBk6).
clues.summary: A valley running north-east to south-west with low mountains, a wide river and, unusually for the country, plenty of trees. Some side roads run through forest.

clues.title: Landscape: one flat-ridge mountain on flat land
text: You can recognise the area near the town of Selfoss from its distinct** flat-ridge mountain**. Due to the otherwise flat landscape, this mountain can be seen from a wide area.
clues.summary: Around a southern town, a distinctive mountain with a flat ridge stands over otherwise flat land and can be seen from far away.

clues.title: City: biggest city, flat, on a bay
text: Reykjavík is the capital and by far the **largest city** in Iceland. The city is mostly flat with slight hills, and is located on the south side of a bay. It is most recognizable as it is significantly larger than other Icelandic cities, with a large urban area and “bigger city” feel.
NOTE: The city of Akureyri can feel urban in some places. You can distinguish it from Reykjavik as it has mountains to the east and west.
clues.summary: The capital is by far the largest city: mostly flat with slight hills, on the south side of a bay, with a big-city feel. The second city can feel urban too but has mountains to its east and west.

clues.title: City: valley town with mountains both sides
text: Akureyri is the second-biggest city in Iceland and is located in a **North-South oriented valley**, along the western edge of the bay. The city features mountains ranges to the [east](https://goo.gl/maps/eMBDTPVRuWi2EmU2A) and [west](https://goo.gl/maps/FyqhMTP1bcbLEqsG9), making it recognisable.
clues.summary: The second biggest city sits in a north-south valley on the west edge of a bay, with mountain ranges to the east and west.

clues.title: Google car: red truck south-west, white north-east
text: Iceland can be split in half depending on the colour of the pickup truck, with red being found in the southwest, and white being found in the northeast.
clues.summary: The country splits by pickup colour: red in the south-west, white in the north-east.

clues.title: Landscape: glaciers reaching toward the sea
text: The southern coast of Iceland features some impressive **glaciers **visible from the ring road, spilling into the sea from the Vatnajökull ice cap.
clues.summary: On the south coast, big glaciers are visible from the ring road, spilling toward the sea from a huge ice cap.

clues.title: Road: divided or multi-lane highway, very rare
text: There are only a handful of highways in Iceland which are either divided or have [more than two lanes](https://goo.gl/maps/9owq3fnCFyQ2AUNc6). The divided highways are shown in dark red, while the highways with three or more lanes are shown in bright red.
NOTE: There are two exceptions to this:

- Divided roads can be found [inside cities](https://www.google.com/maps/@65.6881721,-18.100425,3a,90y,310.87h,91.63t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1saLoFnUFOLKwTHVQjhucjfw!2e0!7i13312!8i6656) other than Reykjavík.
Roads may temporarily be divided close to [intersections](https://www.google.com/maps/@63.9386364,-20.9768781,3a,90y,235.63h,90.36t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1s34lZI1gR3PEmXPVURzpLkQ!2e0!7i13312!8i6656).
clues.summary: Only a handful of highways are divided or have three or more lanes. Exceptions: divided roads inside towns other than the capital, and short divided bits near junctions.

clues.title: Landscape: ragged cliffs over a harbour town
text: The Island of Heimaey can easily be recognised by seeing these [ragged rocky cliffs](https://maps.app.goo.gl/PB2qmrLJhXrFr4cn9) overlooking the town of Vestmannaeyjabær. Similar cliffs can be seen on [the islands off the coast](https://maps.app.goo.gl/zaCCHo6sAfCtyPGt7).
clues.summary: An island recognisable by ragged rocky cliffs above its town. Similar cliffs show on the small islands off the coast.

clues.title: Coverage: very foggy
text: Very **foggy coverage** can be found around the town of Bakkagerði, in northeastern Iceland. The fog can also be seen from a [distance](https://maps.app.goo.gl/3cetMcszhGSG7FJMA).
clues.summary: Very foggy coverage in the north-east around one small town. The fog is visible from a distance too.

clues.title: Road: divided highway southwest of the capital
text: The 41 and 43 southwest of Reykjavík, as well as the 1 between Grundarhverfi and Selfoss are divided.

clues.summary: Roads 41 and 43 southwest of the capital, and road 1 between Grundarhverfi and Selfoss, are divided.
